Chemistry-Fix #1 misconception: intermol.detail: Boiling breaks INTERMOLECULAR forces, NOT covalent bonds. Watch BBC Bitesize 'Simple molecular substances'. Test: explain why H2O boils at 100°C but H-O bonds only break at 2000°C+
Chemistry-Fix #1 misconception: intermol.name: Fix intermolecular vs covalent bond misconception

Chemistry-Learn bond energy calculations.detail: Method: (1) List all bonds in reactants (BREAKING = endothermic +). (2) List all bonds in products (FORMING = exothermic -). (3) Sum: ΔH = bonds broken - bonds formed. Practice with methane combustion.
Chemistry-Learn bond energy calculations.name: Learn bond energy calculations

Chemistry-Learn electrolysis rules: CATi.detail: CATHODE (negative) attracts CATIONS. ANODE (positive) attracts ANIONS. Draw electrolysis cell for aqueous NaCl. Label all ions and products.
Chemistry-Learn electrolysis rules: CATi.name: Learn electrolysis electrode rules

Chemistry-Learn percentage by mass: prac.detail: Steps: (1) Write correct formula (Diya used Fe3O4 instead of Fe2O3!). (2) Calculate Mr. (3) Mass of element = Ar x atoms. (4) Divide x 100. Practice: carbon in CO2, oxygen in H2O, calcium in CaCO3.
Chemistry-Learn percentage by mass: prac.name: Learn percentage by mass calculations

Chemistry-Memorise Required Practical eq.detail: Diya lost a mark for 'Bunsen burner with beaker' instead of 'water bath'. GCSE mark schemes want STANDARD equipment names. List equipment for all 4 Chemistry Required Practicals.
Chemistry-Memorise Required Practical eq.name: Memorise practical equipment names

Chemistry-Memorise definitions: isotope.detail: Diya lost marks describing observations instead of definitions. Flashcards: isotope SAME protons DIFFERENT neutrons. Weak acid = PARTIALLY IONISED. Ionic bond = electron TRANSFER + electrostatic attraction.
Chemistry-Memorise definitions: isotope.name: Memorise key definitions with keywords

Chemistry-Review thermal conduction: del.detail: Metals conduct heat + electricity because of DELOCALISED ELECTRONS (free to move through lattice). This is also why metals are malleable. Link to metallic bonding model.
Chemistry-Review thermal conduction: del.name: Review metallic bonding and thermal conduction

Chemistry-Study hydrogen fuel cells: how.detail: Diya wrote 'Haven't learnt yet'. BBC Bitesize: Fuel cells. Key: H2 → 2H+ + 2e- at anode, O2 + 4H+ + 4e- → 2H2O at cathode. Overall: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O.
Chemistry-Study hydrogen fuel cells: how.name: Study hydrogen fuel cells
